stem: A client with symptomatic heart failure is classified as New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class III. Which assessment finding best matches this classification?

options.A: The client is comfortable at rest but develops heart-failure symptoms with less-than-ordinary physical activity.
options.B: The client has no limitation of physical activity and ordinary activity does not cause heart-failure symptoms.
options.C: The client has slight limitation of physical activity, with symptoms only during ordinary activity.
options.D: The client has heart-failure symptoms at rest and cannot perform any physical activity without discomfort.

rationale: The AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline defines NYHA class III as marked limitation of physical activity: the client is comfortable at rest but develops heart-failure symptoms with less-than-ordinary activity. Class I has no limitation, class II has slight limitation with ordinary activity, and class IV includes symptoms at rest. Therefore, A is the best match.
educational_objective: Identify NYHA class III as marked functional limitation with heart-failure symptoms during less-than-ordinary activity while the client remains comfortable at rest.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_locator: Section 2.1, immediately after Table 3 under 'New York Heart Association (NYHA) Classification': NYHA class III includes patients comfortable at rest who have symptoms of HF with less-than-ordinary activity; class II has symptoms with ordinary activity and class IV has symptoms at rest. The 2026 Second Universal Definition reaffirms the contemporary HF staging framework without replacing this NYHA functional-class construct.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports the symptom and activity pattern defining NYHA functional class III and distinguishes it from classes I, II, and IV.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Physiological Adaptation: assess and recognize changes in functional status and symptoms associated with chronic cardiac conditions and apply pathophysiologic knowledge to client care.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — functional limitation in symptomatic heart failure
correction_summary: Retained the valid NYHA class III construct but replaced vague distractors with the actual neighboring functional-class patterns. The current AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline supplies an exact locator and the final item tests clinical classification rather than rote wording alone.

audit_findings.source_authority: Primary AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure clinical practice guideline.
audit_findings.currentness: The 2022 guideline remains authoritative for the NYHA functional-class definitions; the June 2026 universal definition did not replace this construct.

claim_by_claim.stem: NYHA class III is an appropriate symptom/functional-capacity classification for symptomatic HF.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because it exactly matches the guideline description of class III.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because it describes class I.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because it describes class II rather than marked limitation with less-than-ordinary activity.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because symptoms at rest are class IV.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Uses the exact clinical distinctions without adding unsupported exercise thresholds or quantitative activity measures.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to recognition of NYHA class III.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: Each distractor represents a real neighboring NYHA functional class, making the alternatives clinically plausible and mutually exclusive.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A matches class III; B, C, and D map to classes I, II, and IV respectively.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe activity tolerance and symptom patterns in parallel form.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation remains appropriate because the item tests functional manifestations of chronic HF.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked the exact NYHA definitions in the current guideline and challenged whether 'less-than-ordinary activity' is sufficiently specific. That wording is the guideline distinction for class III and leaves A uniquely correct. No unresolved conflict remains.
